guitar.notes: Corrected: Kim Thayil is Soundgarden's guitarist; Chris Cornell was primarily vocalist (occasionally rhythm guitar) so listing him as co-equal guitarist overstates his role. Kim Thayil's Guild S-100 is reasonably well documented.

tone.target: raw grunge crunch with wah bite and thick low mids
tone.profile: raw grunge crunch with wah bite and thick low mids
tone.summary: A gritty grunge tone achieved using a Marshall-style preamp (UK 45) for punchy crunch, paired with a Wah pedal accent and minimal room ambience.

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and excessive noise inherent in high-gain grunge tones.
Provide initial grit and boost the signal into the high-gain amp section.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here to simulate a dirty, mid-focused overdrive characteristic of grunge crunch, rather than a clean boost.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required wah bite and vocal accent for the riffing.
Add aggressive, saturated crunch and sustain without sounding overly fuzzy.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is chosen for its mid-hump and aggressive saturation, fitting the 'crunch' requirement better than pure fuzz or distortion.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the punchy, mid-focused British Plexi crunch required for classic grunge rock.
Provide the classic British cabinet voicing and punchy low-end response.
Enhance the thick low mids and cut excessive high-end sparkle to maintain a raw, gritty tone.
Add a subtle sense of space (light room) without adding lushness or wash.
blocks.gap: The 'Room' reverb is used sparingly to meet the 'light room' requirement, avoiding excessive decay time.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better cabinet realism and punch.

proposals.reason: Improve the perceived depth and grit of the grunge tone.
